display.title: Episode 439: Torah, the Best Thing of All, Chapter 1
display.summary_short: Children will lead the parade to greet Moshiach, the new song Ad Mosai, a young guest from Ann Arbor, Rabbi Akiva among boastful merchants at sea, and why we smell spices at Havdalah.
display.summary_long: Uncle Yossi opens by telling listeners about the Tzivos Hashem summer newsletter and how to join, and asks them to sign up their friends too. Jewish children will be first to greet Moshiach, proudly reporting how high they have risen in rank, and, as the prophet Daniel foretold, Hashem will send clouds to carry everyone to Eretz Yisroel. He teaches the words of the song 'Ad Mosai' line by line, plays it slowly on his keyboard, and then turns it into the Hakochainik march. An eleven-year-old visitor from Ann Arbor, Michigan recites the Shema and tells about receiving a dollar from the Rebbe for tzedakah. Story time begins with Dovid HaMelech's words that Torah is better than thousands of gold and silver pieces: on a ship full of merchants boasting of gold, silver and diamonds, Rabbi Akiva says his merchandise is worth more than all of it, cannot be stolen and goes wherever he goes. The merchants laugh, and the chapter ends there. Mitzvah time explains why we smell besamim at Havdalah: to comfort us when the extra Shabbos neshamah leaves. A listener's letter about giving tzedakah together leads into the pushka, a sponsor and candle-lighting times.
display.lesson: Torah is the one treasure no one can take away from you; it goes with you wherever you go.
